why: The control plane reads `[sandbox].image` out of a repository's tracked
`.tick/runners.toml` so it can boot what the repository declares (tick x3v).
That makes this Worker a SECOND reader of a format whose first reader is Go,
and a half-applied format fix is invisible when each side is internally
consistent — so both read these cases and must agree on every one.
cloud/factory/test/repo-config.test.ts runs them through the Worker's reader;

cases.name: no sandbox table
cases.why: The 99% path: nothing declared, so the version-pinned base image stands.

cases.name: sandbox table without an image
cases.why: A repository that extends the base image rather than replacing it.
cases.toml:
version = 2

[sandbox]
toolchain = ["rust@1.90.0"]
setup = [
  { command = "cargo fetch", description = "warm the cargo cache" },
]

[roles.implement]
kind = "claude"

cases.name: a digest-pinned image
cases.why: The strongest form the schema's pattern allows.

cases.name: a declaration written as a dotted key
cases.why: Legal TOML for the same table, so a reader that only looks for a [sandbox] header would miss it.

cases.name: a declaration written as an inline table
an image inside another table's multi-line string
cases.why: The reason this is parsed rather than scanned: notes are free text, and a line-oriented reader would boot whatever a note happened to spell.
cases.toml:
version = 2

[testing]
notes = """
when the sandbox is wrong, try:
[sandbox]
image = "not-an-image-anyone-declared"
"""

[testing.commands]
go = { command = "go test ./...", description = "Go" }

[roles.implement]
kind = "claude"

cases.name: a commented-out declaration
cases.why: A comment is documentation, not a declaration.

cases.name: a literal-string declaration with a trailing comment
cases.why: Both readers have to end the value at the quote, not at the newline.

cases.name: an empty image
cases.why: Absent means the base image; empty means the writer meant something and did not say it.

cases.name: a reference that is not a reference
cases.why: An image reference is a name, never a place to hide a shell fragment.

cases.name: an image that is not a string
cases.why: A typed value the schema does not allow is a refusal, not a coercion.
